title: Beyond Plausible Prediction: Safety Sufficiency in Web World Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.40798v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Web world models increasingly predict the consequences of candidate actions before agents act, yet a plausible predicted future does not necessarily support the correct safety decision. In a matched human evaluation of 3,000 predictions from ten frozen open models, 86.1% are judged semantically plausible. However, several models exhibit highly asymmetric authorisation behaviour, combining low false-safe execution with poor recall of clarifiable ASK cases and a strong preference for BLOCK. This motivates safety sufficiency: whether a predictive interface preserves and exposes the policy-decisive information required to distinguish actions that may be EXECUTED, require clarification through ASK, or should be BLOCKED. We introduce SafeWebWorld, a benchmark for evaluating safety sufficiency across five web-safety domains through action-conditioned futures, policy-decisive evidence, and policy-conditioned decisions. translated_title: 超越合理预测：网络世界模型中的安全充分性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.40798v1 公告类型：新 摘要：网络世界模型日益被用于在智能体行动之前预测候选动作的后果，然而一个语义合理的预测未来并不一定能够支持正确的安全决策。在对来自十个冻结开源模型的3,000个预测进行的人类匹配评估中，86.1%的预测被判定为语义上合理。然而，若干模型表现出高度不对称的授权行为：一方面“假安全”（错误放行）执行率较低，另一方面对可澄清的ASK（询问）案例召回率不佳，且强烈倾向于BLOCK（阻止）。这引出了“安全充分性”这一概念：即预测接口是否保留并暴露出区分可执行（EXECUTE）、需要澄清（ASK）或应被阻止（BLOCK）动作所需的策略决定性信息。我们提出了SafeWebWorld基准，通过动作条件化的未来、策略决定性证据和策略条件化的决策，在五个网络（web）安全领域评估安全充分性。在受控的安全……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文揭示网络世界模型即便能给出语义合理的未来预测，也未必支持正确的安全决策，并据此提出“安全充分性”概念及SafeWebWorld基准，用于评估预测接口是否保留了区分执行、询问与阻止动作所需的策略决定性信息。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the concept of "safety sufficiency" and the SafeWebWorld benchmark, showing that plausible predictions in web world models do not necessarily support correct safety decisions, and evaluates whether predictive interfaces preserve the policy-decisive information needed to distinguish EXECUTE, ASK, and BLOCK actions.
